text:
Alex C: Customer reported a burst of 429s around 15:22 UTC despite having burst credits. They saw ~120 rps for ~20s, then 429s. Headers attached: X-Burst-Credits: 0, X-Smoothing-Window: 10s, X-Rate-Limit-Reset: 16s.
Support Bot: Ticket #SR-4952 created and linked to the account. Please add account_id and sample request. :white_check_mark:
Maya S: Can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and the exact response body? Also which plan/account tier is this?
Alex C: repro below — customer calling /v1/completions with batch size 8, concurrency 10. Using api key from sandbox account. Response body snippet: 
```json
{"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded","type":"insufficient_quota","retry_after":16}}
```
Headers: 
```
X-Burst-Credits: 0
X-Burst-Cushion: 0
X-Smoothing-Window: 10
X-Rate-Limit-Limit: 300
X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 0
```

Curl: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small-1","input":"hello","max_tokens":32,"n":8}'
```
Anne (oncall): Quick notes: burst credits are consumed when requests exceed the steady refill. If X-Burst-Credits=0 they have exhausted cushion; smoothing window 10s means short-lived spikes > steady rate will burn credits quickly. Their pattern (10 concurrency * batch 8) multiplies token generation and hits per-second.
DevOps: Also check if they used long-polling or streaming; streaming can hold concurrency slots longer which reduces available throughput.
Maya S: Immediate ask for customer: 1) reduce concurrency to 2-3 and lower batch size to 1-2 to see if 429s stop; 2) implement exponential backoff using Retry-After header; 3) confirm model and avg tokens per request. Please try for 15 minutes and share metrics.
Alex C: Customer did a quick test: set concurrency=2, batch=1 for 10 mins — no 429s. They shared token histogram: avg tokens/request 120.
Anne (oncall): That matches burst exhaustion. Recommendation: short-term mitigation is adjusting concurrency/ batching and backoff. Medium-term: enable smoothing policy change (we can increase smoothing_window to 30s for their tenant) or provision Dedicated/reserved capacity. I can file an internal config change for the account to increase smoothing_window and refill_rate temporarily.
Maya S: Log steps for support reply: explain burst credits model briefly, include repro observed, immediate mitigations (reduce concurrency, lower batch size, backoff with jitter), and options: temporary smoothing_window bump OR move to reserved capacity. Offer 1-hr assisted test with our oncall to adjust tenant smoothing params.
Alex C: Customer agreed to test with lower concurrency and wants the temporary smoothing bump. Shared account_id: acct_81X. Please proceed.
Anne (oncall): I'll open an infra change: request to increase account acct_81X smoothing_window=30s and burst_refill_rate x1.5 for 2 hours starting now. DevOps, please monitor error rate and credits usage.
DevOps: Ack — watching metrics, will report if 429s persist. Should we also recommend they adopt token-level caching / reuse of prompts to reduce avg tokens?
Maya S: Yes add that as best-practice: prefix caching + reuse model where possible. Also note billing impact if they stay at high token volumes; give estimate of cost delta.
Alex C: Thanks team — I'll update customer with steps and the temporary config change. Will paste follow-up here after monitoring window. :thumbsup:
